title: Supermoiré-trapped quadrupolar exciton
authors: Anish Kumar, Suman Chatterjee, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Kausik Majumdar
abstract: Moiré-trapped dipolar interlayer exciton in heterobilayers offers a rich platform to explore interaction-driven phenomena. Extending the number of layers to three and beyond leads to highly intriguing multipolar exciton - a superposition state of vertically aligned phase-coherent excitons. However, in experiments, unintentional twist-angle mismatch among layers may degrade the strength and homogeneity of the vertical Coulomb coupling. Here we propose that the supermoiré effect in a heterotrilayer comes to the rescue by creating periodic pockets of vertically aligned atomic registries that facilitate the formation of quadrupolar excitons trapped in such pockets. Using WS$_2$/WSe$_2$/WS$_2$ stack, we show interaction between multiple confined levels of the top and bottom moiré interfaces, creating electric field tunable multi-level hybridized bright (symmetric) and dark (anti-symmetric) quadrupolar states. Our work underscores the critical role of supermoiré effect in quadrupolar excitons. The discovery of reduced sensitivity on precise angle-alignment will ignite exploration of complex excitonic states in multi-layered heterostructures.
summary: This paper reports on the realization and characterization of supermoiré-trapped quadrupolar excitons in a heterotrilayer. By leveraging the periodic potential from the supermoiré effect, the authors overcome limitations in vertical coupling to create robust QX states. These states are spectroscopically confirmed via unique electric field-dependent optical signatures, highlighting the supermoiré structure's role in controlling complex excitonic physics.
main_problem: The study investigates how the supermoiré effect can facilitate the formation of quadrupolar excitons (QX) in multi-layered heterostructures, overcoming issues caused by unintentional twist-angle mismatch.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that the supermoiré structure creates periodic pockets enabling QX formation, which exhibit distinct non-linear and field-tunable optical signatures compared to simple dipolar excitons.
method: The research combines experimental photoluminescence (PL) measurements on a heterotrilayer with theoretical modeling using Hamiltonians describing exciton hybridization under an applied electric field.
model_or_system: The physical system is a WS2/WSe2/WS2 heterotrilayer exhibiting moiré superlattice effects. The model involves treating the excitons as hybridized states derived from interlayer dipolar excitons (IX) forming quadrupolar exciton (QX) superposition states.
key_observables: PL redshift in trilayers vs. bilayers, non-linear/hyperbolic Stark shift dependence on electric field (F), and changes in circular polarization degree (DOCP).
important_parameters: Electric field strength (F), hybridization energy ($\delta \sim 11.5$ meV), and the supermoiré periodicity.
main_assumptions: The QX formation is robust against slight variations in twist angles due to the supermoiré structure; theoretical analysis often assumes negligible interactions between excitons from different moiré sites for simplification.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the supermoiré landscape, PL spectra showing redshift (trilayer vs. bilayer), and field-dependent shifts: linear shift for IX vs. hyperbolic/non-linear shift for QX.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the physical problem (mismatch degradation) to proposing the supermoiré solution, presenting experimental evidence via PL spectroscopy across varying electric fields, and finally using theoretical models to explain the observed hybridization and field tunability of the resulting quadrupolar states.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it deals with engineered quantum optical systems (excitons) whose properties are dictated by complex moiré potentials and external fields, touching upon concepts used in cavity QED or open quantum system dynamics.
